hero.headline: Zelensky expects major Russian attacks within 48 hours
hero.teaser: The Ukrainian president said intelligence from the U.S. and European allies indicates Russia is preparing a significant offensive.
hero.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects Russia to launch major attacks within the next 48 hours. He said the assessment is based on intelligence shared by the United States and European allies.

Zelensky said the attacks could come at night over the next two days. The Ukrainian government is bracing for what it anticipates will be a significant Russian offensive operation.

cards.headline: Iranian Missile Hits US Base in Kuwait During Peace Talks
cards.body:
US Strike on Iranian Naval Base Kills Over 168, Mostly Children

A video released by Iranian news agency Mehr and verified by the investigative collective Bellingcat shows a US Tomahawk missile striking an Iranian naval compound adjacent to a primary school in Minab on February 28. The strike on the Islamic Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) facility demolished approximately half of the Shajareh Tayyebeh primary school, killing more than 168 people, mostly children aged seven to twelve who were attending morning classes.

The footage and accompanying evidence, including videos verified by the Guardian, photographs from the aftermath, and satellite imagery, indicate that the US was responsible for the school strike while targeting the adjacent IRGC naval compound.

Munitions experts confirm the weapon shown in the video is a Tomahawk missile, which is exclusively used by the US in the current conflict. "The video shows a Tomahawk missile striking a target. Given the belligerents, that indicates it is a US strike, as Israel is not known to possess Tomahawk missiles," said NR Jenzen-Jones, director of Armament Research Services, an intelligence consultancy providing analysis to governments and NGOs. He stated that the munition is clearly not an Iranian Soumar missile, which has a distinctive external engine located on the underside toward the rear.

Satellite imagery of the bombing aftermath reveals at least four buildings were struck: the school and three IRGC compound buildings. The primary school, though once part of the wider IRGC complex, had been walled off from the military compound for at least eight years. The school's educational purpose was evident in satellite images showing playing fields and colorful wall murals.

US military spokespeople stated they are "investigating" the strike. The bombing has drawn international condemnation. UNESCO described it as a "grave violation" of international law, while Human Rights Watch called for the incident to be investigated as a war crime.

The findings directly contradict statements made by President Donald Trump on Sunday. "In my opinion, based on what I've seen, that was done by Iran," Trump said without offering evidence. "They're very inaccurate, as you know, with their munitions. They have no accuracy whatsoever. It was done by Iran."

The strike occurred amid reported ceasefire negotiations between the US and Iran. A report of an extended ceasefire, subject to Trump's approval, led to a decline in global oil prices on Thursday. However, tensions remain high, with both nations trading military strikes despite ongoing diplomatic discussions aimed at reducing hostilities.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran nuclear deal negotiated by his envoys
cards.teaser: President Trump asked for several amendments to a nuclear agreement his envoys reached with Iran during a Situation Room meeting on Friday, according to adminis.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his national security advisers in the Situation Room on Friday to review a nuclear agreement framework that U.S. and Iranian officials had reached. During the meeting, Trump identified several areas where he wanted the deal strengthened, particularly around provisions governing Iran's nuclear material.

The requested amendments have triggered a new round of negotiations between the parties. While Trump's specific proposed changes were not detailed publicly, administration officials characterized them as intended to reinforce the agreement rather than reject it outright.

cards.headline: Eleven Workers Dead in Washington State Chemical Accident
cards.teaser: All bodies have been recovered from a tank implosion at a paper mill in Longview, Washington.
cards.body:
Eleven workers died in a chemical accident at a Nippon paper mill in Longview, Washington. Authorities have recovered and identified all the victims following a tank implosion at the facility.

The incident involved a chemical spill that resulted in the deaths of all workers present. Officials completed recovery operations and released the names of all eleven individuals killed in the disaster at the mill.

cards.headline: Justice Department seeks recusal of judge in Georgia election case
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors say the judge's attendance at an event honoring Fani Willis raises impartiality concerns.
cards.body:
The Justice Department asked a federal judge to recuse herself from overseeing its lawsuit against Georgia election officials. The request came in a filing submitted on Friday to the U.S. District Court.

Prosecutors argued that the judge's attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis raises questions about her ability to remain impartial. The department said her participation in the event creates an appearance of bias in the case.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor steps away from Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: The attorney who secured an indictment against the former FBI director has withdrawn from the case.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has stepped down from the case. A court filing in the Eastern District of North Carolina on Friday announced the substitution.

Comey was indicted for allegedly threatening President Trump's life in a since-deleted social media post featuring seashells. Matthew, the prosecutor who obtained the indictment, filed notice of his withdrawal from the case.

cards.headline: Blue Origin receives national security contract hours before New Glenn rocket explodes
cards.teaser: The company secured a launch task order from the military shortly before its rocket exploded at a Florida launch site.
cards.body:
Blue Origin received a national security launch task order hours before its New Glenn rocket exploded during a test at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night. The massive fireball destroyed the launch pad within seconds of the scheduled hotfire test at 9pm ET. No personnel were harmed, and the company called the explosion an anomaly.

The explosion was visible from 115 miles away in Fort Pierce, where residents reported seeing an orange sky. Blue Origin's CEO confirmed the company has since regained access to the launch complex. The incident affects NASA's lunar plans, which depend on New Glenn launches to support a moon base and human return missions.

hero.headline: Ebola Outbreak Spreads in Democratic Republic of Congo
hero.body:
A severe Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed 65 people, with health officials reporting 246 suspected cases in Ituri province. The situation has drawn urgent international attention, with the head of the World Health Organization visiting the affected region to support containment efforts.

The medical charity Doctors Without Borders has described the spread as deeply alarming. Officials at the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention expressed serious concern about the risk of further transmission, particularly given the geographic location of the outbreak.

Ituri province, which borders Uganda and South Sudan, presents significant challenges for disease control. The region is home to mining towns where populations are highly mobile, with people constantly moving in and out. This mobility makes tracking cases and isolating infected individuals considerably more difficult. Uganda has already confirmed its own outbreak, with a 59-year-old man dying in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the DRC.

The Africa CDC laboratory detected the Ebola virus in 13 of 20 samples tested. The strain identified is the Bundibugyo variety, which presents a particular concern because there is no licensed vaccine available for it. Previous outbreaks of this strain occurred in 2007 and 2012.

The WHO estimates the current outbreak has a death rate between 30 percent and 50 percent based on confirmed cases. As one WHO official explained, this means up to five out of every 10 infected people are likely to die.

Cases have been reported mainly in the Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones, with suspected cases also appearing in the neighboring city of Bunia. The DRC has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was first identified there in 1976, usually involving the Zaire strain.

Experts point to multiple factors contributing to recurring outbreaks in the region. Close human contact with animal reservoirs, likely bats but possibly also primates, is considered a primary source. Other contributing factors include population movement between rural and urban areas, the tropical climate, and extensive rainforest coverage that may harbor the virus.

The Africa CDC has convened an urgent meeting involving authorities from the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan, along with the WHO and pharmaceutical companies. "Rapid regional coordination is essential," said the Africa CDC director general, citing the high population movement between affected areas and neighboring countries.

Ebola spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids of infected people or dead bodies, such as during funeral preparations. The disease causes fever, severe headache, muscle pain, weakness, fatigue, diarrhea, and vomiting, with some cases involving bleeding. Control measures typically include patient isolation, contact tracing, and strict infection control protocols for healthcare workers.

cards.headline: Colombia Holds Presidential Election
cards.teaser: Voters choose between a far-right outsider, a traditional conservative, and the legacy of the country's first leftist president.
cards.body:
Colombia held a presidential election that could reshape relations with the United States, following months of public disputes between left-wing President Gustavo Petro and US President Donald Trump.

The election tested Petro's legacy as Colombia's first leftist leader against a rising far-right outsider and a traditional conservative candidate. The vote also reflected broader tensions over how to address the country's decades-long armed conflict, with candidates offering contradictory proposals for resolution.

cards.headline: Israeli Forces Capture Castle in Lebanon
cards.teaser: The army seized a strategic fortress in its deepest push into Lebanese territory in more than two decades.
cards.body:
Israeli forces captured a strategic castle in Lebanon in the deepest military incursion into the country in 26 years. The operation marked a significant expansion of Israeli military activity across the border.

The seizure of the fortress represented the furthest Israeli ground forces have advanced into Lebanon since 2000. The strategic value of the location and the circumstances of the operation were not specified in available reports.

cards.headline: US Boat Strikes Kill Over 200 in Colombia and Ecuador
cards.teaser: Coastal residents said the airstrike campaign has made many reconsider ocean-based livelihoods.
cards.body:

cards.headline: Hindu Nationalists Elevate 17th-Century Warrior King
cards.teaser: Statues of Shivaji are appearing across India as nationalists reshape the country's identity.
cards.body:
Statues of Shivaji are rising across India as the Hindu right embraces the 17th-century warrior king as a new symbol. The founder of the Maratha empire who fought against the Mughal dynasty now represents the nationalist movement remaking the country.

Demand has soared for figurines and statues of the warrior king, driven partly by a sculptor whose video posted online sparked widespread interest. The proliferation of monuments reflects the growing influence of Hindu nationalist ideology in Indian public life.

cards.headline: Fuel Blockade Disrupts Garbage Collection in Havana
cards.teaser: Even street sweepers cannot escape the impact as trash piles grow across the Cuban capital.
cards.body:
A fuel blockade on Cuba has worsened the lack of consistent garbage pickup in Havana, producing enormous trash piles across the city. The shortage has affected even basic municipal services like street sweeping.

The blockade has aggravated existing problems with waste management in the capital. Fuel shortages prevent regular collection routes, leaving refuse to accumulate in neighborhoods throughout Havana.

cards.headline: Ukraine Appoints Ombudsman to Oversee Soldier Rights
cards.teaser: Olha Reshetylova faces resentment from some commanders but says her work strengthens the armed forces.
cards.body:
The Ukrainian government has tasked Olha Reshetylova with overseeing soldiers' rights, a role that has drawn resistance from some military commanders. She maintains her work strengthens the armed forces despite the pushback.

Ukraine's military does not always welcome criticism, but Reshetylova's position requires her to scrutinize how troops are treated. Some commanders resent her oversight, viewing it as interference in military operations.

cards.headline: Eleven Workers Dead in Washington State Chemical Accident
cards.teaser: All bodies have been recovered from a tank implosion at a paper mill in Longview, Washington.
cards.body:
Eleven workers died in a chemical accident at a Nippon paper mill in Longview, Washington. Authorities have recovered and identified all the victims following a tank implosion at the facility.

The incident involved a chemical spill that resulted in the deaths of all workers present. Officials completed recovery operations and released the names of all eleven individuals killed in the disaster at the mill.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak in DR Congo Raises Alarm
cards.teaser: Medical charity MSF called the spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo deeply concerning.
cards.body:
The Democratic Republic of Congo is experiencing an Ebola outbreak with a death rate between 30% and 50%, according to the World Health Organization. This means up to five out of every ten people infected are likely to die from the virus.

The WHO's director-general has traveled to the Democratic Republic of Congo to support containment efforts. Medical charity Doctors Without Borders has described the situation as deeply alarming, while the WHO chief has called for ceasefires among armed groups to help prevent deaths from the preventable disease.

cards.headline: Former Scottish First Minister Sturgeon Denies Guilt in Embezzlement Case
cards.teaser: Nicola Sturgeon told the BBC she is serving a sentence for a crime she did not commit.
cards.body:
Nicola Sturgeon, Scotland's former first minister, maintained her innocence in her first interview since her estranged husband Peter Murrell pleaded guilty to embezzling 400,000 pounds from the Scottish National Party. Sturgeon told the BBC she is serving a sentence for a crime she did not commit.

During the interview with Laura Kuenssberg, Sturgeon was challenged over the SNP embezzlement scandal. At times during the conversation, the former first minister struggled to hold back tears as she discussed the case.

cards.headline: Spurs Defeat Thunder in Game 7, Advance to NBA Finals
cards.teaser: San Antonio beat defending champions Oklahoma City 111-103 to reach the NBA Finals.
cards.body:
The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals, advancing to the NBA Finals. Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs to victory against the defending champions, who had been heavily favored throughout the season.

The Spurs will now face the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals, with Game 1 scheduled for Wednesday in San Antonio. San Antonio's upset victory ended Oklahoma City's path to a repeat championship.

cards.headline: Hundreds Arrested After Champions League Celebrations in France
cards.teaser: French police arrested hundreds as PSG fans celebrated their team's victory over Arsenal.
cards.body:
Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory over Arsenal sparked widespread unrest across French cities. Hundreds of people were arrested as celebrations turned disorderly, with some fans firing flares into crowds.

Thousands of police officers were deployed to manage the crowds and control the post-match festivities. Their efforts focused on quelling the unrest that erupted during celebrations of PSG's triumph.

cards.headline: Open AI Models Without Safety Controls Becoming More Accessible
cards.teaser: Advanced AI models with no safeguards are now more widely available to users.
cards.body:
Open-weight AI models with advanced capabilities and no built-in safeguards are becoming increasingly accessible to the public. These models are free, private, and designed to fulfill user requests without refusing them.

AI safety experts have expressed concerns about the wider availability of these unrestricted models. While the models offer useful applications across various domains, the absence of safety controls has drawn scrutiny from researchers studying potential risks associated with their deployment.

hero.headline: Anthropic raises $65 billion, surpasses OpenAI in valuation
hero.body:
Anthropic has raised $65 billion in its latest funding round, making the artificial intelligence company more valuable than its rival OpenAI. The Series H funding round values Anthropic at $965 billion after the investment.

The seven cofounders of Anthropic are now worth a combined $116 billion following the funding round. The company develops AI models and tools, competing directly with OpenAI in the artificial intelligence sector.

The massive valuation marks a significant milestone in the ongoing competition between major AI companies. Anthropic has positioned itself as a major player in the artificial intelligence industry through its development of large language models and other AI technologies.

Analyst Dan Ives described Anthropic's growth as just the tip of the spear for the broader AI rally in technology markets. The funding represents one of the largest single investment rounds in the AI sector.

The Series H round brings Anthropic's total funding to substantial levels as investor interest in artificial intelligence companies continues to grow. The company has attracted significant capital from investors betting on the future of AI technology.

Anthropic's valuation now exceeds that of OpenAI, reversing the previous hierarchy in the AI industry. OpenAI has been one of the most prominent names in artificial intelligence following the public release of its ChatGPT product.

The funding comes as competition intensifies among companies developing large language models and other AI systems. Major technology firms and startups are racing to develop more capable AI models and secure market position.

Investors have poured billions of dollars into AI companies over the past year as the technology has moved from research labs into commercial applications. The Anthropic funding round reflects continued confidence in the long-term potential of artificial intelligence technology despite questions about near-term profitability for many AI ventures.

cards.headline: Blue Origin receives national security contract hours before New Glenn rocket explodes
cards.teaser: The company secured a launch task order from the military shortly before its rocket exploded at a Florida launch site.
cards.body:
Blue Origin received a national security launch task order hours before its New Glenn rocket exploded during a test at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night. The massive fireball destroyed the launch pad within seconds of the scheduled hotfire test at 9pm ET. No personnel were harmed, and the company called the explosion an anomaly.

The explosion was visible from 115 miles away in Fort Pierce, where residents reported seeing an orange sky. Blue Origin's CEO confirmed the company has since regained access to the launch complex. The incident affects NASA's lunar plans, which depend on New Glenn launches to support a moon base and human return missions.

cards.headline: United Airlines flight diverted after passenger attempts to breach cockpit
cards.teaser: A passenger on a Chicago to Minneapolis flight made multiple attempts to reach the cockpit, forcing an emergency landing.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted after a passenger repeatedly tried to breach the cockpit. The incident on United flight 2005 prompted a hijacking alert and forced the plane to land in Madison, Wisconsin.

Crew members reported that the passenger made multiple attempts to access the cockpit during the flight. The man was arrested after the plane landed. The FBI stated no criminal charges had been filed yet following the incident.

cards.headline: China factory activity stalls in May as demand weakens
cards.teaser: Manufacturing data shows Chinese industrial production slowed during the month, raising concerns about the broader economy.
cards.body:
Factory activity in China stalled in May as demand weakened across the manufacturing sector. The slowdown raises questions about the health of the Chinese economy and its industrial base.

China's non-manufacturing Purchasing Managers Index rose to 50.1 in May, according to updated figures. The flat factory activity data shows Chinese manufacturers facing headwinds. The manufacturing slowdown serves as a warning sign for the broader Chinese economy.

cards.headline: Joby completes test flight of electric air taxi in New York City
cards.teaser: The aviation startup demonstrated its all-electric aircraft in Manhattan, but public use awaits regulatory approval.
cards.body:
Joby Aviation conducted a test flight of its electric air taxi in New York City, showcasing the all-electric aircraft over Manhattan. The demonstration represents a step toward the company's goal of replacing helicopters with electric vertical takeoff and landing vehicles.

The aircraft cannot yet carry paying passengers. Aviation startups and the Trump administration support replacing helicopters with electric aircraft, but the new vehicles must pass extensive testing before public use. The regulatory approval process remains ongoing for electric air taxis.

cards.headline: Former Marks & Spencer chief to advise government on youth unemployment
cards.teaser: Marc Bolland will help develop strategies to address warnings of a lost generation of young workers.
cards.body:
Marc Bolland, the former chief executive of Marks & Spencer, has been appointed to advise the government on tackling youth unemployment. The role comes following a review that highlighted concerns about a "lost generation" of young people struggling to enter the workforce.

Bolland will provide guidance to help connect young people with employment and training opportunities.

cards.headline: Ferrari faces criticism over first electric vehicle design
cards.teaser: The Luce, intended to compete with Chinese EVs, has drawn backlash from those who say it departs from the brand's heritage.
cards.body:
Ferrari's first electric vehicle, the Luce, has generated criticism following its unveiling. The car was designed to take on Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers in a growing market segment.

Some critics say the Luce abandons Ferrari's traditional design principles and heritage. The backlash has prompted questions about the brand's direction as it enters the electric vehicle market.

hero.headline: Microsoft threatens legal action against security researchers disclosing exploits
hero.body:
Microsoft is facing criticism for threatening legal action against a security researcher who publicly disclosed zero-day exploits affecting the company's software. The dispute centers on how the researcher shared vulnerability information and has reignited debate about responsible disclosure practices in the cybersecurity industry.

A researcher using the alias Nightmare Eclipse has been engaged in a public disagreement with Microsoft over exploit code. Posts suggest the individual may be a former employee of the company. Security researcher Kevin Beaumont drew attention to how Microsoft has responded to these disclosures, triggering widespread coverage across major technology publications.

Microsoft has taken aggressive steps against the researcher, including blocking their GitHub account and threatening criminal investigation. According to reports, the researcher claimed Microsoft representatives stated they could "ruin my life" over the disclosure of security exploits. The researcher subsequently responded to Microsoft's legal threats by pledging what was characterized as a "bone shattering drop," suggesting plans for additional security disclosures.

The conflict highlights longstanding tensions between major software companies and independent security researchers. Researchers typically work to identify vulnerabilities before malicious actors can exploit them. However, the process of disclosing flaws remains contentious within the technology industry, with companies and researchers often disagreeing over timing, methods, and public versus private notification.

Microsoft has not publicly detailed the specific exploits in question or provided detailed legal justification for pursuing the researcher. The company's position centers on claims that certain disclosures violated its policies. GitHub, the platform where Microsoft took action, hosts millions of software projects and is widely used by developers and security professionals worldwide.

The researcher described feeling humiliated by Microsoft's approach, according to reports. Multiple technology news outlets have characterized the company's response as threatening toward someone working in legitimate cybersecurity research.

This incident underscores broader questions about how technology companies should handle security vulnerabilities discovered by independent researchers. Some argue that researchers deserve protection when disclosing flaws responsibly, while companies contend they must protect proprietary systems and control how vulnerability information spreads.

The case also reflects growing concerns about corporate power in the technology sector. Large companies like Microsoft control significant infrastructure and have substantial legal resources, creating potential imbalances when disputes arise with individual researchers.

Security experts have noted that aggressive corporate responses may discourage researchers from reporting vulnerabilities through official channels, potentially pushing disclosure toward more adversarial approaches. The incident raises questions about whether Microsoft's strategy achieves its intended goal of improving security or instead damages relationships with the research community that identifies critical flaws in commercial software products.

cards.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, causes loud booms heard across New England
cards.teaser: A meteor exploded over Massachusetts, creating sonic booms that puzzled residents and were reported from Delaware to Montreal.
cards.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating a blast equivalent to 300 tons of TNT, according to NASA. The fireball broke apart at an altitude of 40 miles while traveling at 75,000 miles per hour.

The explosion generated loud sonic booms that echoed across the region, puzzling residents who heard the unexpected noise.

cards.headline: Nvidia-powered Windows PCs to debut next week
cards.teaser: The first Windows computers powered by Nvidia chips will be unveiled next week, according to Axios.
cards.body:
Nvidia will debut its first processors designed for Windows laptops next week, Axios reported. The new N1X laptop processors represent Nvidia's entry into the Windows PC chip market, according to The Verge.

Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm are all promoting the launch ahead of what Nvidia has described as its biggest event of the year at Computex 2026. Nvidia posted messages on social media ahead of the GTC event. The chips mark a shift for Nvidia, which has primarily focused on graphics processors and data center hardware.

cards.headline: Xbox delays Fable to February 2027
cards.teaser: Microsoft postponed the release of Fable to February 2027, a move attributed to avoiding competition with GTA 6.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced that Fable will launch in February 2027, delaying the game from its previously planned release. Multiple gaming outlets reported the delay is intended to avoid direct competition with Grand Theft Auto 6, according to Pure Xbox and TechPowerUp.

Game Informer and IGN both covered the announcement. The decision represents the second delay for the fantasy role-playing game. Polygon reported that Xbox made the move to avoid a collision with the highly anticipated GTA 6 release.

cards.headline: AC unveils 720-horsepower Cobra Coupe with Ford V8 engine
cards.teaser: British carmaker AC introduced a new Cobra Coupe featuring a supercharged Ford 5.0-liter V8 engine producing up to 720 horsepower.
cards.body:
AC, Britain's oldest active carmaker, debuted a production model of its Cobra Coupe powered by a Ford 5.0-liter V8 engine. The two-seat sports car produces between 720 and 799 horsepower depending on configuration, according to multiple automotive publications.

The vehicle is priced at $315,000 to $500,000 depending on specifications. CarBuzz reported the supercharged supercar features modern engineering while honoring the classic Cobra design. Ford Authority confirmed the official production debut of the Ford-powered model.

cards.headline: James Bond game '007: First Light' records strong 24-hour sales
cards.teaser: The new James Bond video game '007: First Light' became a sales hit in its first day of release.
cards.body:
The video game '007: First Light' achieved impressive sales during its first day on the market. Developed by IO Interactive, the game marks a significant milestone for James Bond video games, which have struggled to find critical success in recent years.

IO Interactive, known for its Hitman stealth series, created the game with attention to detail that reflects the developer's expertise in espionage gameplay. The title follows a young Bond before he becomes agent 007, offering players a fresh take on the iconic character.

cards.headline: Blue micromoon visible this weekend
cards.teaser: A rare blue micromoon, the second full moon of May, rises this weekend.
cards.body:
A blue micromoon will be visible this weekend, combining two astronomical phenomena. Despite its name, the event isn't actually blue or particularly small. A blue moon refers to the second full moon occurring within a calendar month, while a micromoon describes the moon at its farthest point in its orbit.

This rare combination makes for a noteworthy celestial event. The Guardian provides details on what the terms mean and guidance on the best timing to observe the blue micromoon this weekend.

hero.headline: Wembanyama Leads Spurs Past Thunder to NBA Finals
hero.body:
Victor Wembanyama scored 22 points and pulled down seven rebounds as the San Antonio Spurs defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on Saturday night. The victory sends the Spurs to the NBA Finals to face the New York Knicks, with the championship series beginning Wednesday in San Antonio.

Wembanyama was named the Western Conference Finals MVP following his stellar performance throughout the series. The 22-year-old French player became emotional after clinching the Spurs' trip to the finals. "Realizing that some part of a childhood dream is going to come true," he said when explaining his tears. "We're still hungry, we want more. This feeling is so powerful, I can't explain it."

The Spurs' victory came despite the Thunder being the defending NBA champions. However, Oklahoma City played without Jalen Williams, who was sidelined by a hamstring injury. The absence of Williams proved costly as San Antonio sealed the series with a breakaway dunk as the final seconds ticked away.

Wembanyama's teammates provided crucial support throughout the decisive game. Julian Champagnie scored 20 points and made six three-pointers, while backup center Luke Kornet made a crucial defensive play with a block at the rim in the fourth quarter when Oklahoma City threatened a comeback. Young guard Dylan Harper also looked impactful when entering the game off the bench.

After the game, Champagnie credited Wembanyama's presence as a game-changer. "When you've got the greatest player in the world things happen," Champagnie said.

For the Thunder, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning NBA MVP, delivered another dominant performance with 35 points and nine assists. However, no other Oklahoma City player scored more than 20 points, and the defending champions were unable to overcome the Spurs' balanced attack.

Thunder coach Mark Daigneault acknowledged the difficult loss but remained optimistic about his team's future. "You have to grow from every experience, including the tough ones," he said. "And it's the NBA, there are tough ones. We can also be really disappointed. There's nobody that we don't think we can beat, respectfully."

The NBA Finals matchup between San Antonio and New York will mark a rematch of their 1999 meeting, when the Spurs defeated the Knicks 4-1 to win the championship. This will be the Spurs' first NBA Finals appearance in several years and their bid for their sixth franchise title. The Knicks are seeking their first championship since 1973.

cards.headline: Claude Lemieux's Family to Donate Brain for CTE Research
cards.teaser: The family of former NHL star Claude Lemieux will donate his brain to Boston University's CTE Center.
cards.body:
The family of Claude Lemieux announced they will donate his brain to the Boston University CTE Center for research. Police confirmed the former NHL player died by suicide.

Lemieux played professional hockey for multiple teams during his career. His family's decision to donate his brain will contribute to ongoing research into chronic traumatic encephalopathy and its effects on athletes.

cards.headline: Amanda Serrano Ties Women's Boxing Knockout Record
cards.teaser: Amanda Serrano stopped Cheyenne Hanson in the second round to equal the record for most knockouts in women's boxing history.
cards.body: Amanda Serrano retained her WBA and WBO featherweight titles by defeating Cheyenne Hanson in a second-round stoppage in Texas. With this victory, Serrano equaled the all-time record for most knockouts in women's boxing history, cementing her place among the sport's elite competitors.

cards.headline: Hundreds Arrested After Champions League Celebrations in France
cards.teaser: French authorities arrested hundreds following unrest during celebrations of PSG's Champions League victory over Arsenal.
cards.body:
Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory over Arsenal sparked widespread unrest across France. Police deployed thousands of officers to manage celebratory crowds, some of whom set off flares in the streets.

Authorities arrested hundreds of people as they worked to control the disruptive celebrations. The disturbances spread across multiple areas as PSG fans marked their team's win.

cards.headline: AB Hernandez Wins California State Track Titles
cards.teaser: Transgender athlete AB Hernandez won two state championship medals at the California track and field meet.
cards.body:
AB Hernandez, a transgender senior from Jurupa Valley, won two state track and field medals at the California championships, capping off her high school career.

The competition drew protests, though they remained subdued during the event itself.

cards.headline: Tyler Fletcher Joins Scotland World Cup Squad
cards.teaser: Manchester United teenager Tyler Fletcher will replace the injured Billy Gilmour in Scotland's World Cup squad.
cards.body:
Manchester United teenager Tyler Fletcher has been called up to Scotland's World Cup squad as a late replacement for Billy Gilmour, who suffered a knee injury during a pre-tournament friendly against Curaçao.

Scotland will compete in the World Cup for the first time in 28 years, with Haiti as their opening opponent. Fletcher's addition comes after the squad's 3-0 victory over 10-man Curaçao, which ended on a disappointing note with news of Gilmour's injury ruling him out of the tournament.

cards.headline: Illinois Legislature Delays Bears Stadium Decision
cards.teaser: The proposed stadium deal for the Chicago Bears did not advance on the final day of the Illinois legislative session.
cards.body:
The Chicago Bears stadium proposal moved to the back burner as the Illinois legislative session concluded. The state Senate and House faced a key deadline but did not advance the stadium funding legislation.

Lawmakers rolled out a $55 billion budget plan but the Bears stadium bill broke down before the legislative deadline. The delay leaves the future of the team's proposed stadium project uncertain as the session ended.

hero.headline: Alaskan Bush People Star Matt Brown Dead at 42
hero.body:
Matt Brown, a cast member of the Discovery Channel reality series Alaskan Bush People, has died at 42. His brother Noah helped pull his body from a river.

Brown had been spotted near a river where authorities later reported a man went missing. A search for Brown was called off after dangerous storm conditions made recovery efforts unsafe.

Brown appeared on Alaskan Bush People alongside his family members. The show followed the Brown family living in remote areas of Alaska and later Washington state. Matt Brown was one of several siblings featured on the program, which began airing in 2014.

The circumstances surrounding Brown's presence at the river have not been detailed in available reports. His brother Bear Brown had previously indicated that Brown was likely dead after being seen in the area where the body was recovered.

Brown's death marks the second loss for the Bush People family in recent years. The family's patriarch, Billy Brown, died in 2021 at age 68. The show had documented the family's off-grid lifestyle and various challenges they faced living in wilderness areas.

The Discovery Channel has not released a statement regarding Brown's death. The show has aired for multiple seasons and developed a dedicated audience interested in the family's unconventional way of life.

Matt Brown had been open about personal struggles in past seasons of the show. He had taken breaks from filming at various points during the series' run. His brothers Noah and Bear have both been active on social media but have not provided additional details about the incident beyond confirming the recovery of his body from the river.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remainder of 2026 Tour to Focus on Health
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old Four Seasons frontman has canceled all remaining concerts on his farewell tour.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli has canceled the remainder of his 2026 farewell tour concerts, citing health concerns. The 92-year-old singer announced he needs to focus on his health and apologized to fans for the disappointment.

Valli had been performing as part of a farewell tour with the Four Seasons. The group achieved fame in the 1960s with hits that later became the subject of the Broadway musical Jersey Boys. The canceled dates represented the final scheduled performances of the year.

cards.headline: Italy Bans Kanye West and Travis Scott Concerts Over Security Concerns
cards.teaser: Planned July concerts in Reggio Emilia have been prohibited by Italian authorities.
cards.body:
Kanye West's concert scheduled for July 18 at the RCF Arena in Reggio Emilia, Italy has been cancelled by the city's prefect Salvatore Angieri. The decision cited public order and safety issues as the reason for the ban.

The cancellation came after concerns raised by the local Jewish community regarding West's previous antisemitic remarks. West, who changed his name to Ye in 2021, was set to perform at the Pulse of Gaia festival in the northern Italian city.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Removes Second Contestant in Two Years Over Racial Slur
cards.teaser: Vasana Montgomery will not appear on the reality show after old social media posts surfaced.
cards.body:
Love Island USA has removed cast member Vasana Montgomery from the upcoming season after offensive social media posts surfaced. She will not appear when the show returns to Peacock on June 2, just two days after the Season 8 cast announcement.

This marks the second consecutive year the reality dating series has dismissed a contestant over similar social media posts containing offensive language.

cards.headline: Donald Trump Offers to Perform at Freedom 250 Concert After Artists Cancel
cards.teaser: The former president suggested performing himself after multiple musicians backed out of the event series.
cards.body:
Donald Trump has offered to headline the Freedom 250 concert himself after several performers withdrew from the event. Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride all backed out, citing concerns that the event would become political.

Trump responded to the artist departures by suggesting the concert series cancel its music performances altogether. Vanilla Ice was among the few artists who defended his continued participation, arguing that music should have no political boundaries. Trump is now set to perform at the associated Great American State Fair following the wave of cancellations.

cards.headline: Warner Bros. Executive Warns Against Cutting Development Budgets
cards.teaser: Michael De Luca said reducing investment in original material could dry up studio pipelines.
cards.body:
Warner Bros. Pictures chief Michael De Luca cautioned studio executives against making deep cuts to development budgets for original material. Speaking at the Producers Guild of America's Produced By conference, he warned that excessive cost-cutting threatens to deplete creative pipelines needed for long-term production.

De Luca emphasized the strategic importance of investing in new talent and fresh voices to maintain a robust development slate. He framed this commitment to nurturing original material as essential for sustaining the studio's future production capabilities.

cards.headline: Only Murders in the Building Wins CrimeCon Award for Scripted Series
cards.teaser: Hulu led the 2026 CrimeCon Clue Awards with two major category wins.
cards.body:
Hulu's Only Murders in the Building won the award for outstanding scripted series at the 2026 CrimeCon Clue Awards. The streaming platform also took home the prize for outstanding docuseries with Girl on the Run: The Hunt for Americas Most Wanted.

The winners were announced at the annual awards ceremony recognizing crime-focused programming. Hulu led all platforms with two major category wins at the event.

hero.headline: Zelensky expects major Russian attacks within 48 hours
hero.teaser: The Ukrainian president said intelligence from the U.S. and European allies indicates Russia is preparing a significant offensive.
hero.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects Russia to launch major attacks within the next 48 hours. He said the assessment is based on intelligence shared by the United States and European allies.

Zelensky said the attacks could come at night over the next two days. The Ukrainian government is bracing for what it anticipates will be a significant Russian offensive operation.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran nuclear deal negotiated by his envoys
cards.teaser: President Trump asked for several amendments to a nuclear agreement his envoys reached with Iran during a Situation Room meeting on Friday, according to adminis.
cards.body:
President Trump met with his national security advisers in the Situation Room on Friday to review a nuclear agreement framework that U.S. and Iranian officials had reached. During the meeting, Trump identified several areas where he wanted the deal strengthened, particularly around provisions governing Iran's nuclear material.

The requested amendments have triggered a new round of negotiations between the parties. While Trump's specific proposed changes were not detailed publicly, administration officials characterized them as intended to reinforce the agreement rather than reject it outright.

cards.headline: Blue states propose 100 percent tax on anti-weaponization fund payments
cards.teaser: State lawmakers want to tax payments from Trump's fund for people targeted by what he calls political prosecutions.
cards.body:
Several blue states are proposing legislation to impose a 100 percent tax on payments from President Trump's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund, which was created to compensate individuals Trump says were targeted by political prosecutions.

The fund has generated significant backlash since its announcement, including divisions within the Republican Party. A New York lawmaker stated that anyone who participated in the Capitol riot and receives money from the fund would lose those payments through taxation. Democratic-led states view the proposals as a way to prevent what they characterize as rewarding criminal behavior. A judge has agreed to review the fund.

cards.headline: Federal judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: A judge agreed to examine the fund created to compensate people Trump says were victims of political prosecutions.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Miami has reopened a $10 billion lawsuit that President Trump and his sons filed against the Internal Revenue Service, stemming from a 2013 leak of their personal and business tax returns by a former contractor.

The judge's decision came after a third-party motion challenged the settlement that created the $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund, arguing it lacked sufficient detail and represented potential collusion and fraud. The fund, announced this month to compensate individuals Trump says were targeted by political prosecutions, has sparked significant backlash and exposed divisions within the Republican Party.

cards.headline: Justice Department seeks recusal of judge in Georgia election case
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors say the judge's attendance at an event honoring Fani Willis raises impartiality concerns.
cards.body:
The Justice Department asked a federal judge to recuse herself from overseeing its lawsuit against Georgia election officials. The request came in a filing submitted on Friday to the U.S. District Court.

Prosecutors argued that the judge's attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis raises questions about her ability to remain impartial. The department said her participation in the event creates an appearance of bias in the case.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor steps away from Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: The attorney who secured an indictment against the former FBI director has withdrawn from the case.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has stepped down from the case. A court filing in the Eastern District of North Carolina on Friday announced the substitution.

Comey was indicted for allegedly threatening President Trump's life in a since-deleted social media post featuring seashells. Matthew, the prosecutor who obtained the indictment, filed notice of his withdrawal from the case.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor and DHS secretary coordinate on ICE facility protests
cards.teaser: State police were deployed to maintain order outside a Newark detention center amid escalating demonstrations.
cards.body:
Protests at the Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark have intensified, with a hunger and labor strike by detained immigrants entering its ninth day. The demonstrators are demanding improved conditions and medical care at the facility.

State police deployed barricades to separate opposing groups outside the center on Saturday. Pro-immigration protesters faced off against Trump-supporting counterprotesters who demonstrated in support of ICE operations. The escalating demonstrations prompted coordination between New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to manage the situation.
